facts.text: Maracanã Stadium, opened in 1950, hosted the 1950 World Cup final where Uruguay beat Brazil in the historic Maracanazo.
The stadium also served as the venue for the opening and closing ceremonies of the 2016 Olympic Games, lighting up Rio’s night sky.
Maracanã neighborhood derives its name from the Tupi–Guarani word for “green bird,” reflecting the area’s lush vegetation.
The Maracanã metro station, on Line 2, sits directly beside the stadium, making it one of the few stations that opened with the 2016 Games.
The stadium’s roof is a tensioned membrane canopy that covers the main stands, a design feature added during the 2014 World Cup renovation.
The Maracanã neighborhood hosts the UERJ, one of Rio’s main universities, and its main avenue, Maracanã Avenue, links it to Tijuca.
